//: Type checking only — esbuild does the bundling and strips types without ever checking them,
so without this pass a genuine type error ships silently as a runtime crash.
`noEmit` because nothing here produces output; the build script owns that.
`strict` is on deliberately. The rules layer is full of small integers that all look alike —
a square, a piece, a move, a colour are every one of them a `number` — and strict null
checking is the only thing standing between 'this square is empty' and 'this square is a
white pawn' when a lookup misses.
